whatItIs: Compiled code, indexes and previews Xcode keeps for your projects.
whySafe: Xcode makes it from your source code, which stays untouched.
howItComesBack: Xcode rebuilds it on the next build; that build takes longer.

whatItIs: Debug symbols Xcode copied from each iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch or Apple TV you connected.
whySafe: They're copies of what's on the device.
howItComesBack: Xcode copies them again the next time you connect that device.

whatItIs: Simulated iPhones, iPads and Android phones, and the system images they run.
whySafe: Xcode and Android Studio can create or download them again. Apps and data inside a device go with it.
howItComesBack: Create the device again, or download the runtime in Xcode or Android Studio.

whatItIs: Libraries your projects downloaded: node_modules, Pods, Python environments and the like.
whySafe: Each project lists what it needs, so nothing of yours is lost.
howItComesBack: Your package manager installs them again (npm install, pod install, pip install…).

whatItIs: Compiled files and build caches inside your projects.
whySafe: They're made from your source code, which stays untouched.
howItComesBack: Made again on your next build.

whatItIs: Packages and downloads that package managers and build tools keep so they don't fetch them twice.
whySafe: They're copies of what's online; your projects say what they need.
howItComesBack: Downloaded again the next time a build or install needs them.

whatItIs: Installed versions of languages, SDKs and developer tools, and the browsers test tools download.
whySafe: Each can be installed again with the tool that put it there. A project may still need one, so Sōji never ticks them.
howItComesBack: Reinstall it with its version manager or SDK manager when a project needs it.

whatItIs: Caches and indexes that editors, IDEs and coding tools keep to start faster.
whySafe: The tools rebuild them; your projects and settings stay.
howItComesBack: Rebuilt the next time the tool opens a project.

whatItIs: Extension folders of VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf, including versions an update left behind.
whySafe: An extension you still use goes with its folder, so Sōji never ticks them. Old versions are safe to remove.
howItComesBack: Install the extension again from the editor.

whatItIs: Disks of virtual machines and container engines: Docker, OrbStack, UTM, Parallels and others.
whySafe: A machine's files and settings go with it, so Sōji never ticks them. Remove machines you no longer use.
howItComesBack: Images download again; a removed machine has to be set up again.

whatItIs: Machine learning models and datasets that AI tools and apps downloaded.
whySafe: They're downloads; the tool fetches a model again when you use it.
howItComesBack: Downloaded again the next time you run that model.

whatItIs: Files apps keep to load faster: web pages, thumbnails, artwork and updates waiting to install.
whySafe: Apps rebuild their caches as needed; your documents and settings stay.
howItComesBack: Rebuilt as you use the app, which may be a little slower at first.

whatItIs: Files apps, builds and agents left in the temporary folders.
whySafe: They're meant to be thrown away, and macOS clears them on its own.
howItComesBack: The app that made one makes it again if it needs it.

whatItIs: Records apps write while they run, and reports from past crashes.
whySafe: Nothing needs them to work; they're only for troubleshooting.
howItComesBack: Apps write new ones as they run.

whatItIs: Render, proxy and preview files that video, photo and audio apps make from your media.
whySafe: They're made from your original media, which stays.
howItComesBack: The app makes them again when you open the project.

whatItIs: Instruments, loops, samples and sound packs that music apps downloaded.
whySafe: The app can download them again, so Sōji never ticks them.
howItComesBack: Download them again from the app's sound library.

whatItIs: Games and mods that game launchers installed.
whySafe: Their launcher can install them again, so Sōji never ticks them. Check your saves are backed up first.
howItComesBack: Install it again from your launcher's library.

whatItIs: Episodes and media apps downloaded to play offline.
whySafe: The app streams them, or downloads them again while they're still published.
howItComesBack: Download it again in the app. Episodes a show took down don't come back.

whatItIs: Installers, disk images and archives you downloaded, and updates kept for later.
whySafe: What they installed keeps working, and most can be downloaded again.
howItComesBack: Download it again from where it came from.

whatItIs: Backups of iPhones and iPads, and the archives Xcode makes for each app release.
whySafe: A backup may be the only copy, so Sōji never ticks them. Remove ones you no longer need.

whatItIs: Photos, videos and files received in WhatsApp and Signal.
whySafe: This may be the only copy, so Sōji never ticks them. Remove only what you've saved elsewhere.

whatItIs: Large videos, recordings and video projects in your folders.
whySafe: They're your own files, so Sōji never ticks them. Remove only what you don't need.

whatItIs: Older saved versions of your documents, kept by apps that save as you work.
whySafe: Sōji keeps each document, its newest older version and any conflict. A removed version can't be restored.

whatItIs: Files you moved to the Trash.
whySafe: Sōji ticks them only with Tick old items in the Trash on. Emptying the Trash removes them for good.

whatItIs: Copies of your repositories that coding agents made to work on a task.
whySafe: Sōji keeps any with uncommitted or unmerged work; the rest is already in your repository.
howItComesBack: The agent makes a new one for its next task.

whatItIs: Transcripts of past coding agent sessions, and the state editors keep per project.
whySafe: Sōji takes only sessions left idle a while, never a running one. A removed session can't be resumed.

whatItIs: Data and settings left by apps you removed, and by older versions of apps you updated.
whySafe: Reinstalling the app would use them, so Sōji never ticks them. Remove leftovers of apps you won't reinstall.

whatItIs: Your libraries, mail, messages, keychains and macOS's own files.
whySafe: Sōji never removes these.
